title: Total exports (goods + services)
definition: Combined merchandise and services exports for the fiscal year, as reported by the Department of Commerce.
notes: FY2024-25 was first reported at $820.93 bn and later revised to $825.26 bn as late services returns came in. Services export data is estimated monthly and revised for up to a year.
Growth is now almost entirely services-led. Merchandise exports grew 0.93% in FY2025-26 against 8.71% for services.

title: Merchandise exports
definition: Value of physical goods exported during the fiscal year.
notes: Effectively flat in FY2025-26. This is the clearest single sign that 'Make in India' has not yet converted into export competitiveness in goods.
Petroleum products remain a large share, which makes the headline sensitive to crude prices rather than manufacturing capability.

title: Services exports
definition: Value of services exported during the fiscal year, including software, business and financial services.
notes: India's genuine global strength. Telecom/computer/information services alone were $206.6 bn — about 49% of services exports.
Concentration is also the risk: roughly half of services exports sit in one sector exposed to AI-driven automation of exactly that work.

title: Services exports by segment
definition: Breakdown of services export value by major category, FY2025-26.

points.note: Residual: total 421.32 less the two named segments.

title: GDP, nominal
definition: Gross domestic product at current market prices in US dollars.
notes: India is the 5th largest economy by nominal GDP as of 2025, behind the US, China, Germany and Japan — not 4th, a claim that circulates widely but did not hold at the time of verification.
Nominal dollar GDP moves with the exchange rate. Rupee depreciation has repeatedly masked real growth in this series.
Per-capita GDP, not total GDP, is the meaningful development measure — see the benchmark page.

points.note: Implied by the reported 5.19% increase to 2025.
